title: Rabbi Dostai of Biri
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: (Biri is a town in Babylonia, as in Eruvin 56a.) Hyman finds him mentioned in halakhah only in Avodah Zarah 40a: Ulla raised a contradiction to Rabbi Dostai of Biri from what Rav said, “fish entrails and their roe” …; he answered him, “Delete ‘their roe’ from here.” Rabbi Zeira said to him, “Do not delete it.”

In aggadah we find in Eruvin 45a that he expounded “What is the meaning of what is written, ‘And they told David’?”; in Bava Kamma 83a he expounded the verse “And when it rested he would say” — that the Divine Presence does not rest upon Israel when they are fewer than two thousand and two myriads, etc.; and in Sanhedrin 107a he expounded: “To what is David like? To a merchant — that my sin not be written … He said to him: And the yod that I took from Sarai stood and cried out for many years until Joshua came and I added it to him,” etc.

notes.text: Saved Davidson Avodah Zarah40a reads רמי ליה: Ulla raises a contradiction to Dostai, who answers by deleting roe; Zeira says not to delete it. No spokesman appointment is supported. The original contrary note is superseded, all prior versions preserved.

The consulted Avodah Zarah 40a directly has Ulla raising a contradiction to Dostai, followed by deletion of roe and Zeira’s objection. The former spokesman-appointment interpretation remains historical and is not reinstated. Hyman’s only-halakhah assertion, Biri location and other homily reports remain his scope claims.
